newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rejigged Anglovaal seen luring foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Rejigged Anglovaal seen luring foreigners.

text.p: Winning shareholders' nod to restructure, Anglovaal Ltd hopes to revel in the growth and exploration opportunities its two new arms will offer it in Africa into the next century, analysts said on Thursday.

They added that the group's new structure should prove attractive to international investors who baulk at the complicated holding structure and management contracts of traditional South African mining houses and mines.
Anglovaal's gold holdings will be grouped into a single unit called Avgold and the group's minerals and mining investments will fall under the umbrella of a second unit, Avmin.
Both arms are set to be listed on December 30 on the Johannesburg and Brussels stock exchanges.

"The overseas investor knows the structure of groups like Barrick (Gold Corp). He doesn't really understand the South African system of listing separate mines and a holding company," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Anglovaal spokesman Julian Gwyllim agreed international investors would be more familiar with the new structure.

Anglovaal on Wednesday won shareholder approval for its restructuring. Approval was won only after Anglovaal agreed to appoint independent non-executive directors to the Avgold board to bring management in line with that of international firms.
"We are aiming for an extremely focused and incentivised management team," Gwyllim said.
Some shareholders were initially opposed to the cancellation of Anglovaal's management contracts with the individual mines.
But analysts say that the cancellation of management contracts and fees will likely lure international investors.
With a streamlined management strategy, Avgold and Avmin were seen growing rich on any future opportunities arising.

Avgold will combine into one company about 72 million ounces of potential gold resources as well as the 62.2 million ounces already controlled by the Anglovaal gold mines. The unit will have a total gold output of 1.1 million ounces per year.
Avgold hopes to swell total annual output to 1.5 million ounces by 2005 and to reduce average total production costs to below $200 per ounce from $285 per ounce.

"With a consolidated strategy and combined cash resources strategy, Avgold can make the most of any opportunities arising in South Africa and across the borders. There is growth that will come from African exploration," an analyst said.
But Anglovaal's Gwyllim said that at this stage any exploration and development would remain in Africa.
Avmin is currently very active in Zambia's copperbelt area.

The group has an option to participate in the Konkola North exploration, it held much property for exploration in the copperbelt and was interested in some of Zambia's soon-to-be privatised mining companies.
Avgold's immediate focus would be in South Africa's northern Free State before turning to the rest of Africa, he said.
"Avgold has what in the market could be called critical mass. It's large enough to be a main player," Gwyllim said.
Avgold will comprise Eastern Transvaal Consolidated Mines, Loraine Gold Mines Ltd and Target Exploration Co Ltd, as well as Target's Sun and Oribi projects.
Middle Witwatersrand (Western Areas) will be the vehicle for holding the minerals and mining investments.
